<content>
1: # opencode-container
2: 
3: Docker images for running [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) in various serving modes — HTTP server, web UI, ACP protocol bridge, and ephemeral issue-processing workers.
4: 
5: ## Quickstart
6: 
7: ```bash
8: # 1. Build all images
9: make build
10: 
11: # 2. Start the headless HTTP server
12: make serve
13: 
14: # 3. Verify it's running
15: curl -u "opencode:changeme" http://localhost:4096/global/health
16: ```
17: 
18: **Prerequisites**: [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/) (with Compose v2), [gh CLI](https://cli.github.com/) (for runner containers).
19: 
20: ## Containers
21: 
22: | Container | Mode | Port | Purpose |
23: |---|---|---|---|
24: | `opencode-serve` | `serve` | 4096 | Headless HTTP server with web UI + REST API + OpenAPI doc |
25: | `opencode-web` | `web` | 4098 | Same as serve with auto-instantiated project instance |
26: | `opencode-acp` | `acp` | 4097 | ACP (Agent Client Protocol) JSON-RPC server over stdio, bridged to TCP via socat |
27: | `opencode-issue-processor` | `run` | — | Batch: iterate all open issues from configured repos, piped into `opencode run` |
28: | `opencode-plan-issue` | `run` | — | One-shot: clone a repo, analyze an issue, post implementation plan as comment |
29: | `opencode-generic-worker` | `run` | — | Clone a repo, bootstrap opencode config, execute a mounted script or inline command |
30: 
31: ## Architecture
32: 
33: ### Why this design?
34: 
35: OpenCode supports three runtime modes — `serve` (HTTP API), `web` (HTTP + instant project), and `acp` (JSON-RPC stdio) — plus a `run` mode for one-off agent invocations. Each mode has different network and lifecycle needs:
36: 
37: - **`serve` / `web`** are long-running HTTP servers. They bind to a port, persist data in Docker volumes, and expose health-check and API endpoints.
38: - **`acp`** communicates over stdio using JSON-RPC 2.0. To make it accessible over the network inside Docker, `socat` bridges the stdio protocol to a TCP socket. This allows external ACP clients to connect without modifying the opencode process.
39: - **`run` containers** (`issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker`) are ephemeral. They clone a git repo, perform a task via `opencode run`, and exit. They use Docker's `profiles: [manual]` so they are never started by `docker compose up` — only via explicit `docker compose run --rm`.
40: 
41: ### Which container do I pick?
42: 
43: | You want to... | Use this container |
44: |---|---|
45: | Run a headless OpenCode server with a web UI | `opencode-serve` |
46: | Run OpenCode web with an auto-created project | `opencode-web` |
47: | Connect an ACP client (e.g., Cline, continue.dev) | `opencode-acp` |
48: | Process all open issues from one or more repos | `opencode-issue-processor` |
49: | Analyze a single issue and post a plan | `opencode-plan-issue` |
50: | Run a custom script inside a cloned repo | `opencode-generic-worker` |
51: 
52: ### Volume sharing strategy
53: 
54: All containers that persist configuration or data share two named volumes:
55: 
56: | Volume | Mount point | Contents |
57: |---|---|---|
58: | `opencode-data` | `/root/.local/share/opencode` | Session data, project history |
59: | `opencode-config` | `/root/.config/opencode` | Global opencode config, agent definitions |
60: 
61: This means data and configuration persist across container restarts and can be shared between server and runner containers.
62: 
63: ### `profiles: [manual]` pattern
64: 
65: Containers with `profiles: [manual]` are excluded from `docker compose up`. They must be launched explicitly with `docker compose run --rm`. This prevents long-running server mode from accidentally starting ephemeral batch containers.
66: 
67: ## Environment Variables
68: 
69: | Variable | Affected containers | Required | Default | Security note |
70: |---|---|---|---|---|
71: | `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` | `opencode-serve`, `opencode-web` | no | `changeme` | Basic auth password for HTTP endpoints |
72: | `GH_TOKEN` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker` | yes (for GitHub operations) | — | Interpolated by calling shell via `$(gh auth token)` — never read into agent context |
73: | `ISSUE_URL` | `plan-issue` | yes | — | Full GitHub issue URL (e.g. `https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/42`) |
74: | `REPO_URL` | `generic-worker` | yes | — | Git clone URL |
75: | `ISSUE` | `generic-worker` | no | empty | Issue number, passed as env to child command |
76: | `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` | `generic-worker` (script) | no | `/opencode-config` | Directory to copy config from when bootstrapping |
77: | `WORK_DIR` | `generic-worker` (script) | no | `/repo` | Clone destination directory |
78: | `OPENCODE_GLOBAL_DIR` | `generic-worker` (script) | no | `/root/.config/opencode` | Target directory for bootstrapped config |
79: | `TARGETARCH` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker` (Docker build ARG) | no | `amd64` | Architecture for `gh` CLI binary download (`amd64` or `arm64`). Set via `docker build --build-arg TARGETARCH=arm64` |
80: | `ARCH` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker` (derived in RUN) | — | — | Internal variable derived from `TARGETARCH` inside Dockerfile RUN commands. Not user-configurable. |
81: 
82: ## Network
83: 
84: | Container | Port | Auth |
85: |---|---|---|
86: | `opencode-serve` | 4096 | Basic auth via `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` |
87: | `opencode-web` | 4098 | Basic auth via `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` |
88: | `opencode-acp` | 4097 | None (stdio → TCP via socat) |
89: 
90: ## Commands
91: 
92: ```bash
93: make build      # docker compose build
94: make run        # docker compose up -d (all servers)
95: make stop       # docker compose down
96: make serve      # docker compose up -d opencode-serve
97: make web        # docker compose up -d opencode-web
98: make acp        # docker compose up -d opencode-acp
99: make logs       # docker compose logs -f
100: make clean      # docker compose down --remove-orphans -v
101: make process    # docker compose run --rm opencode-issue-processor
102: make plan       # docker compose run --rm opencode-plan-issue
103: make generic    # docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker
104: make lint       # shellcheck on all .sh files
105: make test       # Run integration tests for all containers
106: ```
107: 
108: ## Usage
109: 
110: ### Server containers (long-running)
111: 
112: ```bash
113: # Start all servers
114: make run
115: 
116: # Start individual server
117: docker compose up -d opencode-serve
118: 
119: # Health check
120: curl -u "opencode:changeme" http://localhost:4096/global/health
121: 
122: # View logs
123: make logs
124: 
125: # Stop everything
126: make stop
127: ```
128: 
129: ### Issue processor (batch, then exit)
130: 
131: ```bash
132: GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) make process
133: ```
134: 
135: The processor iterates all open issues from configured repos (see `process-issues.sh`), running `opencode run` on each.
136: 
137: ### Issue planner (one-shot, then exit)
138: 
139: ```bash
140: ISSUE_URL=https://github.com/tbrandenburg/pyrag/issues/30 \
141:   GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) \
142:   make plan
143: ```
144: 
145: Clones the repo, analyzes the issue, and posts an implementation plan as a GitHub comment.
146: 
147: ### Generic worker (one-shot, clone + exec)
148: 
149: ```bash
150: # Mount a local script and execute it in the cloned repo:
151: docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker \
152:   -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/tbrandenburg/pyrag.git \
153:   -e ISSUE=42 \
154:   -v ./workflows/issue-resolution/.opencode:/opencode-config:ro \
155:   -v ./my-script.sh:/script.sh:ro \
156:   /script.sh
157: 
158: # Pass an inline command instead:
159: docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker \
160:   -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/tbrandenburg/pyrag.git \
161:   -e ISSUE=42 \
162:   sh -c 'echo "Issue: $ISSUE" && cat README.md'
163: ```
164: 
165: All runner containers pass `GH_TOKEN`, `ISSUE_URL`, `REPO_URL`, and `ISSUE` from the host environment as-is — they never enter agent context.
166: 
167: ### `--help` passthrough
168: 
169: ```bash
170: docker compose run --rm opencode-serve --help
171: docker compose run --rm opencode-web --help
172: ```
173: 
174: ## Rules & Security
175: 
176: - Only `opencode serve` and `opencode web` support `--port`, `--hostname`, `--cors`, `--mdns`
177: - `opencode acp` communicates over stdio using JSON-RPC 2.0 — socat bridges it to TCP for container access
178: - `opencode run` is used for ephemeral batch/plan containers — needs a git repo and provider credentials
179: - **Never hardcode `GH_TOKEN`** in Dockerfiles or scripts. Use `$(gh auth token)` from the calling shell.
180: - All containers use `node:22-slim` base image with `opencode-ai` npm package and `gh` CLI installed via tarball from `cli/cli` releases
181: - `profiles: [manual]` services must be run with `docker compose run --rm` — not started by `docker compose up`
182: - Container `CMD` / `ENTRYPOINT` scripts use `set -euo pipefail` and validate required environment variables with meaningful error messages before proceeding
183: 
184: ## Testing
185: 
186: ```bash
187: make build    # Build all images first
188: make test     # Run integration tests
189: ```
190: 
191: The test suite exercises:
192: - `--help` passthrough for `opencode-serve` and `opencode-web`
193: - Required env-var validation for `generic-worker`
194: - Clone-and-inspect workflow for `generic-worker` against a real public repo
195: 
196: ## License
197: 
198: MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

(End of file - total 198 lines)
</content>

# opencode-container

Docker images for running [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) in various serving modes — HTTP server, web UI, ACP protocol bridge, and ephemeral issue-processing workers.

## Quickstart

```bash
# 1. Build all images
make build

# 2. Start the headless HTTP server
make serve

# 3. Verify it's running
curl -u "opencode:changeme" http://localhost:4096/global/health
```

**Prerequisites**: [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/) (with Compose v2), [gh CLI](https://cli.github.com/) (for runner containers).

## Containers

| Container | Mode | Port | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `opencode-serve` | `serve` | 4096 | Headless HTTP server with web UI + REST API + OpenAPI doc |
| `opencode-web` | `web` | 4098 | Same as serve with auto-instantiated project instance |
| `opencode-acp` | `acp` | 4097 | ACP (Agent Client Protocol) JSON-RPC server over stdio, bridged to TCP via socat |
| `opencode-issue-processor` | `run` | — | Batch: iterate all open issues from configured repos, piped into `opencode run` |
| `opencode-plan-issue` | `run` | — | One-shot: clone a repo, analyze an issue, post implementation plan as comment |
| `opencode-generic-worker` | `run` | — | Clone a repo, bootstrap opencode config, execute a mounted script or inline command |

## Architecture

### Why this design?

OpenCode supports three runtime modes — `serve` (HTTP API), `web` (HTTP + instant project), and `acp` (JSON-RPC stdio) — plus a `run` mode for one-off agent invocations. Each mode has different network and lifecycle needs:

- **`serve` / `web`** are long-running HTTP servers. They bind to a port, persist data in Docker volumes, and expose health-check and API endpoints.
- **`acp`** communicates over stdio using JSON-RPC 2.0. To make it accessible over the network inside Docker, `socat` bridges the stdio protocol to a TCP socket. This allows external ACP clients to connect without modifying the opencode process.
- **`run` containers** (`issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker`) are ephemeral. They clone a git repo, perform a task via `opencode run`, and exit. They use Docker's `profiles: [manual]` so they are never started by `docker compose up` — only via explicit `docker compose run --rm`.

### Which container do I pick?

| You want to... | Use this container |
|---|---|
| Run a headless OpenCode server with a web UI | `opencode-serve` |
| Run OpenCode web with an auto-created project | `opencode-web` |
| Connect an ACP client (e.g., Cline, continue.dev) | `opencode-acp` |
| Process all open issues from one or more repos | `opencode-issue-processor` |
| Analyze a single issue and post a plan | `opencode-plan-issue` |
| Run a custom script inside a cloned repo | `opencode-generic-worker` |

### Volume sharing strategy

All containers that persist configuration or data share two named volumes:

| Volume | Mount point | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `opencode-data` | `/root/.local/share/opencode` | Session data, project history |
| `opencode-config` | `/root/.config/opencode` | Global opencode config, agent definitions |

This means data and configuration persist across container restarts and can be shared between server and runner containers.

### `profiles: [manual]` pattern

Containers with `profiles: [manual]` are excluded from `docker compose up`. They must be launched explicitly with `docker compose run --rm`. This prevents long-running server mode from accidentally starting ephemeral batch containers.

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Affected containers | Required | Default | Security note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` | `opencode-serve`, `opencode-web` | no | `changeme` | Basic auth password for HTTP endpoints |
| `GH_TOKEN` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker` | yes (for GitHub operations) | — | Interpolated by calling shell via `$(gh auth token)` — never read into agent context |
| `ISSUE_URL` | `plan-issue` | yes | — | Full GitHub issue URL (e.g. `https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/42`) |
| `REPO_URL` | `generic-worker` | yes | — | Git clone URL |
| `ISSUE` | `generic-worker` | no | empty | Issue number, passed as env to child command |
| `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` | `generic-worker` (script) | no | `/opencode-config` | Directory to copy config from when bootstrapping |
| `WORK_DIR` | `generic-worker` (script) | no | `/repo` | Clone destination directory |
| `OPENCODE_GLOBAL_DIR` | `generic-worker` (script) | no | `/root/.config/opencode` | Target directory for bootstrapped config |
| `TARGETARCH` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker` (Docker build ARG) | no | `amd64` | Architecture for `gh` CLI binary download (`amd64` or `arm64`). Set via `docker build --build-arg TARGETARCH=arm64` |
| `ARCH` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker` (derived in RUN) | — | — | Internal variable derived from `TARGETARCH` inside Dockerfile RUN commands. Not user-configurable. |

## Network

| Container | Port | Auth |
|---|---|---|
| `opencode-serve` | 4096 | Basic auth via `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` |
| `opencode-web` | 4098 | Basic auth via `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` |
| `opencode-acp` | 4097 | None (stdio → TCP via socat) |

## Commands

```bash
make build      # docker compose build
make run        # docker compose up -d (all servers)
make stop       # docker compose down
make serve      # docker compose up -d opencode-serve
make web        # docker compose up -d opencode-web
make acp        # docker compose up -d opencode-acp
make logs       # docker compose logs -f
make clean      # docker compose down --remove-orphans -v
make process    # docker compose run --rm opencode-issue-processor
make plan       # docker compose run --rm opencode-plan-issue
make generic    # docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker
make lint       # shellcheck on all .sh files
make test       # Run integration tests for all containers
```

## Usage

### Server containers (long-running)

```bash
# Start all servers
make run

# Start individual server
docker compose up -d opencode-serve

# Health check
curl -u "opencode:changeme" http://localhost:4096/global/health

# View logs
make logs

# Stop everything
make stop
```

### Issue processor (batch, then exit)

```bash
GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) make process
```

The processor iterates all open issues from configured repos (see `process-issues.sh`), running `opencode run` on each.

### Issue planner (one-shot, then exit)

```bash
ISSUE_URL=https://github.com/tbrandenburg/pyrag/issues/30 \
  GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) \
  make plan
```

Clones the repo, analyzes the issue, and posts an implementation plan as a GitHub comment.

### Generic worker (one-shot, clone + exec)

```bash
# Mount a local script and execute it in the cloned repo:
docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker \
  -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/tbrandenburg/pyrag.git \
  -e ISSUE=42 \
  -v ./workflows/issue-resolution/.opencode:/opencode-config:ro \
  -v ./my-script.sh:/script.sh:ro \
  /script.sh

# Pass an inline command instead:
docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker \
  -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/tbrandenburg/pyrag.git \
  -e ISSUE=42 \
  sh -c 'echo "Issue: $ISSUE" && cat README.md'
```

All runner containers pass `GH_TOKEN`, `ISSUE_URL`, `REPO_URL`, and `ISSUE` from the host environment as-is — they never enter agent context.

### `--help` passthrough

```bash
docker compose run --rm opencode-serve --help
docker compose run --rm opencode-web --help
```

## Rules & Security

- Only `opencode serve` and `opencode web` support `--port`, `--hostname`, `--cors`, `--mdns`
- `opencode acp` communicates over stdio using JSON-RPC 2.0 — socat bridges it to TCP for container access
- `opencode run` is used for ephemeral batch/plan containers — needs a git repo and provider credentials
- **Never hardcode `GH_TOKEN`** in Dockerfiles or scripts. Use `$(gh auth token)` from the calling shell.
- All containers use `node:22-slim` base image with `opencode-ai` npm package and `gh` CLI installed via tarball from `cli/cli` releases
- `profiles: [manual]` services must be run with `docker compose run --rm` — not started by `docker compose up`
- Container `CMD` / `ENTRYPOINT` scripts use `set -euo pipefail` and validate required environment variables with meaningful error messages before proceeding

## Testing

```bash
make build    # Build all images first
make test     # Run integration tests
```

The test suite exercises:
- `--help` passthrough for `opencode-serve` and `opencode-web`
- Required env-var validation for `generic-worker`
- Clone-and-inspect workflow for `generic-worker` against a real public repo

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# opencode-container

Docker images for running [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) — an AI coding agent — in every supported mode: HTTP server, web UI, ACP protocol bridge, and ephemeral issue-processing workers.

## Quickstart

**Prerequisites**: [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/) (with Compose v2), [gh CLI](https://cli.github.com/) (for runner containers).

```bash
make build
make serve
curl -u "opencode:changeme" http://localhost:4096/global/health
```

That's it. Three commands, zero edits, and you have a running OpenCode server.

## Containers

| Container | Dockerfile | Mode | Port | Profiles | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `opencode-serve` | `serve.dockerfile` | `serve` | 4096 | — | Headless HTTP server: web UI + REST API + OpenAPI doc. Starts with an initialized git project. |
| `opencode-web` | `web.dockerfile` | `web` | 4098 | — | Same as `serve` but uses `opencode web` (auto-instantiates a project on first load). |
| `opencode-acp` | `acp.dockerfile` | `acp` | 4097 | — | ACP (Agent Client Protocol) JSON-RPC server over stdio, bridged to TCP via `socat`. For ACP-compatible clients (Cline, continue.dev). |
| `opencode-issue-processor` | `issue-processor.dockerfile` | `run` | — | `manual` | Batch: iterates all open issues from configured repos, pipes each into `opencode run`. Exits when done. |
| `opencode-plan-issue` | `plan-issue.dockerfile` | `run` | — | `manual` | One-shot: clones a repo, analyzes a specific issue, posts an implementation plan as a GitHub comment. Exits when done. |
| `opencode-generic-worker` | `generic-worker.dockerfile` | `run` | — | `manual` | Clone a repo, bootstrap opencode config from a mounted volume, execute a mounted script or inline command. |

### Which container do I pick?

| You want to... | Use |
|---|---|
| Run a headless OpenCode server with a web UI | `opencode-serve` (`make serve`) |
| Run OpenCode web with an auto-created project | `opencode-web` (`make web`) |
| Connect an ACP client (e.g. Cline, continue.dev) | `opencode-acp` (`make acp`) |
| Process all open issues from one or more repos | `opencode-issue-processor` |
| Analyze a single issue and post a plan | `opencode-plan-issue` |
| Run a custom script inside a cloned repo | `opencode-generic-worker` |
| Pass `--help` flags to opencode | `docker compose run --rm opencode-serve --help` |

## Architecture

### Why this design?

OpenCode supports three runtime modes — `serve` (HTTP API), `web` (HTTP + instant project), and `acp` (JSON-RPC over stdio) — plus a `run` mode for one-off agent invocations. Each mode has different network and lifecycle requirements:

- **`serve` / `web`** are long-running HTTP servers. They bind to a port, persist data in Docker volumes, and expose health-check and API endpoints. They use `ENTRYPOINT ["opencode", "serve|web"]` with `CMD` for default flags, so `--help` passthrough works naturally.

- **`acp`** communicates over stdio using JSON-RPC 2.0. To make it accessible over the network inside Docker, `socat` bridges the stdio protocol to a TCP socket (`socat TCP-LISTEN:4097 EXEC:"opencode acp"`). This allows external ACP clients (Cline, continue.dev) to connect without modifying the opencode process — it works on any port without opencode knowing about it.

- **`run` containers** (`issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker`) are ephemeral. They clone a git repo, perform a task via `opencode run`, and exit. They use `profiles: [manual]` so they are never started by `docker compose up` — only via explicit `docker compose run --rm`. This prevents accidental startup of batch containers alongside long-running servers.

### The profile/manual pattern

```yaml
profiles:
  - manual
```

Containers with `profiles: [manual]` are excluded from `docker compose up` and `make run`. They must be launched explicitly:

```bash
docker compose run --rm opencode-plan-issue
```

This guarantees that ephemeral batch containers never accidentally stay running.

### Volume sharing strategy

All persistent containers share two named Docker volumes:

| Volume | Mount point | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `opencode-data` | `/root/.local/share/opencode` | Session data, project history, LLM conversation logs |
| `opencode-config` | `/root/.config/opencode` | Global opencode config, agent definitions, custom prompts |

This means:
- Data survives container restarts and rebuilds
- Server and runner containers share the same config and history
- Volumes are created automatically by `docker compose up`

### Base image

All containers use `node:22-slim` with:
- `opencode-ai` npm package installed globally (`npm install -g opencode-ai@latest`)
- `gh` CLI installed from GitHub releases tarball (runner containers only)
- `git`, `ca-certificates` for clone operations
- `socat` for the ACP bridge container

### Network ports

| Container | Host port | Container port | Protocol | Auth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `opencode-serve` | 4096 | 4096 | HTTP | Basic auth via `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` |
| `opencode-web` | 4098 | 4098 | HTTP | Basic auth via `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` |
| `opencode-acp` | 4097 | 4097 | TCP (JSON-RPC) | None (stdio → TCP via socat) |

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Affected containers | Required | Default | Security note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` | `opencode-serve`, `opencode-web` | no | `changeme` | HTTP Basic auth password. Override in docker-compose.yml or via `-e`. |
| `GH_TOKEN` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker` | yes (for GitHub operations) | — | GitHub personal access token. Pass via `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token)` at runtime. Never hardcoded in any Dockerfile or script — only interpolated by the calling shell. Never enters agent context. |
| `ISSUE_URL` | `plan-issue` | yes | — | Full GitHub issue URL, e.g. `https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/42`. The script parses owner/repo/number from this URL. |
| `REPO_URL` | `generic-worker` | yes | — | Git clone URL. The generic worker validates this is non-empty before proceeding. |
| `ISSUE` | `generic-worker` | no | empty | Issue number passed as an environment variable to the child command or script. |
| `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` | `generic-worker` | no | `/opencode-config` | Source directory (inside container) to copy config from when bootstrapping. Mount a host config directory here to inject custom agents. |
| `WORK_DIR` | `generic-worker` | no | `/repo` | Destination directory for `git clone`. |
| `OPENCODE_GLOBAL_DIR` | `generic-worker` | no | `/root/.config/opencode` | Target directory for bootstrapped opencode global config. |
| `TARGETARCH` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker` | no (build ARG) | `amd64` | Docker build `--build-arg` for architecture-specific `gh` CLI download. Set `--build-arg TARGETARCH=arm64` on ARM hosts. |
| `ARCH` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker` | — | — | Internal variable derived from `TARGETARCH` in Dockerfile RUN commands. Not user-configurable. |

### Env var security rules

- `GH_TOKEN` is **never hardcoded** in any Dockerfile or `.sh` file. It is passed at container runtime from the calling shell's `gh auth token` output.
- `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` has a default value of `changeme` in both Dockerfiles and `docker-compose.yml`. Change it in production.

## Commands

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `make install` | No-op (containers are self-contained). Prints informational message. |
| `make build` | `docker compose build` — builds all container images. |
| `make run` | `docker compose up -d` — starts all server containers in background. |
| `make stop` | `docker compose down` — stops all containers. |
| `make serve` | `docker compose up -d opencode-serve` — start only the headless server. |
| `make web` | `docker compose up -d opencode-web` — start only the web UI server. |
| `make acp` | `docker compose up -d opencode-acp` — start only the ACP bridge. |
| `make logs` | `docker compose logs -f` — follow logs from all running containers. |
| `make clean` | `docker compose down --remove-orphans -v` — stop and remove all containers, networks, and volumes. |
| `make process` | `docker compose run --rm opencode-issue-processor` — run the issue processor (exit when done). |
| `make plan` | `docker compose run --rm opencode-plan-issue` — run the issue planner (exit when done). |
| `make generic` | `docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker` — run the generic worker (exit when done). |
| `make lint` | `shellcheck ./*.sh` — static analysis on all shell scripts. |
| `make test` | Build + shellcheck + integration tests for all containers. |

### --help passthrough

Because the serve/web containers use the pattern `ENTRYPOINT ["opencode", "serve|web"]` with `CMD` for flags, you can pass `--help` directly:

```bash
docker compose run --rm opencode-serve --help
docker compose run --rm opencode-web --help
```

## Usage

### Server containers (long-running)

```bash
# Build everything
make build

# Start all servers
make run

# Start individual server
docker compose up -d opencode-serve

# Health check
curl -u "opencode:changeme" http://localhost:4096/global/health

# View logs
make logs

# Stop everything
make stop
```

### Issue processor (batch, then exit)

```bash
GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) make process
```

The processor (`process-issues.sh`) iterates all open issues from hardcoded repos, piping each issue number into `opencode run`. Configure which repos to scan by editing `process-issues.sh`.

### Issue planner (one-shot, then exit)

```bash
ISSUE_URL=https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/30 \
  GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) \
  make plan
```

The planner (`plan-issue.sh`) parses the issue URL to extract owner/repo/number, clones the repo, then pipes a prompt into `opencode run` instructing it to read the issue, understand the codebase, and post a plan as a GitHub comment.

### Generic worker (one-shot, clone + exec)

```bash
# Mount a local script and execute it in the cloned repo:
docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker \
  -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/owner/repo.git \
  -e ISSUE=42 \
  -v ./workflows/issue-resolution/.opencode:/opencode-config:ro \
  -v ./my-script.sh:/script.sh:ro \
  /script.sh

# Pass an inline command instead:
docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker \
  -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/owner/repo.git \
  -e ISSUE=42 \
  sh -c 'echo "Issue: $ISSUE" && cat README.md'
```

The worker (`generic-worker.sh`):
1. Validates `REPO_URL` is set
2. Clones the repo to `WORK_DIR` (default `/repo`)
3. If `/opencode-config` exists (from a mounted volume), copies it to `OPENCODE_GLOBAL_DIR` to bootstrap custom agent definitions
4. Exports `ISSUE` as an environment variable
5. Executes the provided command (or exits with clone info if no command given)

**Security**: `GH_TOKEN`, `ISSUE_URL`, `REPO_URL`, and `ISSUE` are passed from the host environment and never read into agent context.

## Testing

```bash
make build    # Build all images first (required)
make test     # Run shellcheck + all integration tests
```

The test suite (`tests/`) exercises:

| Test file | What it validates |
|---|---|
| `test-serve.sh` | `opencode-serve --help` returns help text |
| `test-web.sh` | `opencode-web --help` returns help text |
| `test-acp.sh` | socat binary is present, opencode binary is present |
| `test-generic-worker.sh` | Missing `REPO_URL` triggers error; clone-and-inspect on a real public repo |
| `test-issue-processor.sh` | Missing `GH_TOKEN` triggers error |
| `test-plan-issue.sh` | Missing `ISSUE_URL` triggers error |

### Running individual tests

```bash
bash tests/test-serve.sh
bash tests/test-generic-worker.sh
```

## Security Rules

1. **Never hardcode `GH_TOKEN`** in Dockerfiles or scripts. Always pass via `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token)` from the calling shell.
2. **Change the default password** in production: set `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` to a strong value.
3. **`profiles: [manual]`** containers must be run with `docker compose run --rm` — never started by `docker compose up`.
4. **Container entrypoints use `set -euo pipefail`** and validate required environment variables before proceeding.
5. **Secrets never enter agent context** — runner containers pass tokens as env vars only, not as part of agent prompts.

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Minimum version | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/) | 24+ (Compose v2) | Container runtime |
| [gh CLI](https://cli.github.com/) | 2.x | GitHub authentication for runner containers |

Docker must be installed and the Docker socket accessible. The `gh` CLI is only required if you use the runner containers (`issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker`).

## Project Structure

```
.
├── serve.dockerfile          # HTTP server image
├── web.dockerfile            # Web UI server image
├── acp.dockerfile            # ACP protocol bridge image
├── issue-processor.dockerfile # Batch issue processor image
├── plan-issue.dockerfile      # Single-issue planner image
├── generic-worker.dockerfile  # Generic clone-and-exec worker image
├── generic-worker.sh          # Entrypoint script for generic-worker
├── plan-issue.sh              # Entrypoint script for plan-issue
├── process-issues.sh          # Entrypoint script for issue-processor
├── docker-compose.yml         # All service definitions, volumes, profiles
├── Makefile                   # All make targets (build/run/test/lint/clean)
├── tests/                     # Integration test suite
├── workflows/                 # Workflow harness definitions
└── AGENTS.md                  # Project-level agent instructions
```

## Dockerfiles detail

### Base pattern (all containers)

```dockerfile
FROM node:22-slim
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    git ca-certificates [socat] [curl] && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
RUN npm install -g opencode-ai@latest
```

### Serve & Web

```dockerfile
ENV OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD=changeme
EXPOSE 4096
ENTRYPOINT ["opencode", "serve"]
CMD ["--port", "4096", "--hostname", "0.0.0.0"]
```

### ACP

```dockerfile
EXPOSE 4097
CMD socat TCP-LISTEN:4097,reuseaddr,fork EXEC:"opencode acp",pty,stderr
```

No `ENTRYPOINT` — uses `CMD` directly so socat is the main process.

### Runner containers (issue-processor, plan-issue, generic-worker)

```dockerfile
ARG TARGETARCH
RUN case "$TARGETARCH" in ... download gh CLI ... esac
COPY *.sh /usr/local/bin/
CMD ["/usr/local/bin/script.sh"]  # or ENTRYPOINT for generic-worker
```

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

8. **Onboarding Self-Service (target 8)**: Prerequisites section in README. `make build` works from clean checkout. `make test` output shows all passing tests.
